description.new:
Barulho World returns to Annex, bringing a curated night to Dortmund that moves between club culture and global sonic landscapes.

As a collective, Barulho World stands for a perspective on
electronic music that centers Afro-diasporic influences
and connects local scenes with international currents.

The musical focus lies on
Afro-electronic sounds
in their full range: from Afrohouse and
Afrotech
to
Gqom
,
Baile Funk
and
Kuduro
, extending into genre-crossing hybrid forms. Rather than fixed categories, the emphasis is on music as a connecting force.

A key part of this approach is the integration of live and hybrid elements. Through hardware, performative setups, or voice, the music remains immediate and closely tied to the moment. The dancefloor becomes not only a space for listening, but for experiencing performance itself.

With Frau Beji, Piccell and D[Nowhere]J, different perspectives come together, each embodying this approach and shaping the space both sonically and emotionally.

Admission 25 €

description.new:
A night shaped by
experimental Detroit techno
, genre-bending selections and a steady awareness of the dancefloor. Moving from hypnotic and stripped-back
techno
into
house
,
jungle
and raw machine-driven rhythms.
For nearly ten years,
Callshop Radio
has been broadcasting live to the world. What began in a backyard in Düsseldorf as part of the interdisciplinary cultural space ROOOOOM has, over the years, evolved into an established community radio, building studios in Leipzig, Paris, and Vienna. The
diversity of genres
reflects the many facets of the scenes that Callshop Radio calls home.

Alongside its ongoing radio program, events have always been a core part of the collective. Collaborations with festivals, clubs, museums, and concert venues create opportunities to bring the station’s hosts onto the stage beyond the studio. The focus remains on connecting artists from different locations and shaping events collaboratively.

On June 13, the radio stays true to this vision: for the Annex Floor at Open Ground, alongside one guest and two residents from the Düsseldorf and Leipzig locations have been invited.

Admission 25 €

description.new:
Mzansi Bass at Open Ground
celebrates the launch of the forthcoming compilation of the same name, curated by Shannen SP, to be released with Colombian label Tratratrax on the 12th of June.

Built with
100% new material
, Mzansi Bass centers artists pushing the boundaries of
bass music in South Africa
, spotlighting the continuum of
radical invention
coming out of the region’s electronic sphere. Exploring the
hypnotic, darker, bassier sounds
in between
3-step, Gqom and experimental Amapiano
to form a succinct snapshot of the country’s unique
soundsystem culture
. Deeply rooted in
Black African rave music
from the local scenes of Durban, Johannesburg, Cape Town, and Pretoria, Shannen describes it as
“electronic music that is embodied, trance inducing and deeply physical.”

With a powerful line up featuring artists on the compilation, this party presents a unique offering of
bass music
. Durban’s gqom icon DJ Lag, who has collaborated with artists ranging from Moses Boyd to Novelist to Ape Drums and has taken his intoxicating brand of
Gqom
to clubs all over the world, from Seoul, to Colombia to New York. Shannen SP, whose sets platform the
vanguard of the global club underground
with recent tours in India and East Asia, and support slots for Arca, Batu and Jamie XX. State OFFF, the Zimbabwe-born and Amsterdam-based artist who has been igniting dancefloors worldwide with his bold productions and high-energy sets, blending
Gqom, Baile Funk, Dubstep, and other global sounds
, earning him a spot on Mixmag’s „Top 25 Artists to Watch in 2025.“

Expect to hear
boundary pushing club music
,
hybrid genres
and
lots of unreleased material
.

Admission 20 € / before 23:00 15 €
description.old:
Mzansi Bass, curated by Shannen SP explores the hypnotic, darker, bassier corners of club music coming out of South Africa and the African continent, covering genres like Gqom, 3 Step, Bacardi - to hybrid sounds that defy categorisation. With a powerful line up featuring Durban’s gqom icon DJ Lag, who has collaborated with artists ranging from Moses Boyd to Novelist to Beyonce and has taken his trance inducing brand of Gqom to clubs all over the world, from Seoul, to Colombia to New York, this party presents a unique offering of bass centred club music. Shannen SP is a creative hybrid who platforms the global club underground. As a DJ, she has supported Arca, Batu, Jamie XX (and warmed up for Bjork), with her commitment to platforming non-western electronic music spanning her A&R work with Hyperdub, NTS and Spitfire Audio. Zimbabwe-born and Amsterdam-based artist State OFFF has been igniting dancefloors worldwide with his bold productions and high-energy sets, blending Gqom, Baile Funk, Dubstep, and other global sounds, earning him a spot on Mixmag’s "Top 25 Artists to Watch in 2025." Expect to hear cutting edge club music, hybrid genres and lots of unreleased material.
Admission 20 € / before 23:00 15 €

strives to carve out spaces for musical expressions which challenge familiar forms,
motivated by an unwavering desire to bring attention to the unnoticed

Subtle Wreck grows from a desire
to deepen the presence of diasporic electronic music
in European contexts, moving beyond the obvious and making space for more layered, experimental, and unsettled approaches to sound.

Together,

channel their shared ambitions to curate a night that invites you to indulge in
lurching amplitudes
and
unexpected danceability
. Through live performances and DJ sets, the invited artists twist the frameworks of
post-club
and
leftfield bass
into a
kaleidoscope of abrasive sound
that refuses to quiet down.

description.new:
1986 music’s core is essentially rooted in the Drum and Bass but since its inception, it has grown freely, breaking down genre barriers and inviting cross pollination.
The essence of the collective encourages artists to experiment in areas they may not be familiar with, allowing for the spectrum to be broad and open. This is reflected in our label events with DJ sets covering many angles whilst retaining our identity. Playing those weird records, testing that new idea….
Our sound is modern and focussed on low end frequencies. What better way to hear those on one of the most reputable spaces in Europe? The primary focus in the space being sound reflects our ethos and we’re excited to experience that with everyone in the room.
Having longer sets on the night will allow each artist to really dig deep and treat the night as a journey.
SP joins us for a DJ set, bringing his own take on UK Garage / 2step, moving in and out of those lines. Alongside, we have Cesco who blurs genres with his minimalist productions and eclectic sets. A regular at Open Ground and 1985 events, Tasha returns with her genre defying sets tinged in Jungle, D&B, Techno and more. Last but not least, Alix debuts at Open Ground for a mixed set that motions through a hybrid collection of Dubstep/Garage/Techno infused tracks, as well as deep, soulful and rolling Drum and Bass that he is primarily known for.
​
Admission 30 €
description.old: Admission 30 €

description.new:
Freifeld: Pin and Doo go way back, and SnPLO (PLO Man, DJ Spence, Sentena) are pleased to join with Doo Montreal studio mate DJ Frog and special guest XDB at Open Ground to DJ party music for people to turn up to in their own way. It’s always hard to describe music with words but basically it’s party music and it’s deep too. Pin and Doo party the same way where we’re trying to be aware of what is going on in the room and get the loop going into something that rolls on its own. But there’s so much more to want from a party and a space.. What will the strengths be? But at the same time we want it to feel like a house party if that’s right. We don’t need it too formal despite all the angles in there. We’re going to be lugging some new records on the train - come early if you want to buy one and chat?…..
​Hopefully it can be the kind of thing where someone can come on their own and have fun, or feel like it wouldn’t be weird to come get in the mix. We’ll be out there too. Like in a way we’ll dissolve, like gatorade powder in water. But also really we’ll all just show up and do our thing because that’s all we can do.

Week-End Music is a Cologne-based platform comprising Week-End Fest - an annual festival that brings together Cologne's local music scene with outstanding international artists - and Week-End Records, founded in 2021, which will celebrate its 25th release this year.

At the heart of both is a deep love for music in all its forms, connecting exciting new talents and legendary musicians. Over the course of 15 years Week-End Fest has welcomed artists like A Certain Ratio, ESG, Suzanne Ciani, Scientist, Adrian Sherwood, Laurel Halo, The Fall, Carl Craig, and New York disco legend Nicky Siano, to only name a few. This year’s 15th anniversary will happen from from November 5-7 in Cologne.

For its first takeover at Annex, Week-End Fest presents a handpicked selection of favourite DJs from Cologne - Sharlipseon, Anna Cainelli, Nikity and DJ Ass Tits - joined by Week-End Records label mate Neue Grafik from London.

Admission 20 € / before 23:00 15 €

description.new:
Cotch International is a club series, record label and curatorial platform which aims to joins the dots between global expressions of soundsystem culture, and platform emerging electronic music scenes from the margins of society. Looking at the soundsystem as a totem around which communities congregate, where resistance is solidified and new sonic and social identities are formed, Cotch has long been a pioneer of non-western club evolutions in the UK scene, operating predominately from South London over the last 10 years.

As they prepare to take over the Annex room on the 15th of August, they have prepared a special all night collaboration between Spanish trailblazer JASSS - one of the most unpredictable, breathtaking and versatile DJs currently doing it - and Cotch resident and co-founder, Joe Cotch. Taking in everything from industrial dub to blistering kuduro beats, swampy trip hop to blown-out baile funk, slinky low end psychedelia and chest-boxing basslines.. everything will be thrown in the blender as they endeavour to move your body in ways you never thought possible.

Admission 40 €

Freifeld: 1986 music’s core is essentially rooted in the Drum and Bass but since its inception, it has grown freely, breaking down genre barriers and inviting cross pollination.
The essence of the collective encourages artists to experiment in areas they may not be familiar with, allowing for the spectrum to be broad and open. This is reflected in our label events with DJ sets covering many angles whilst retaining our identity. Playing those weird records, testing that new idea….
Our sound is modern and focussed on low end frequencies. What better way to hear those on one of the most reputable spaces in Europe? The primary focus in the space being sound reflects our ethos and we’re excited to experience that with everyone in the room.
Having longer sets on the night will allow each artist to really dig deep and treat the night as a journey.
SP joins us for a DJ set, bringing his own take on UK Garage / 2step, moving in and out of those lines. Alongside, we have Cesco who blurs genres with his minimalist productions and eclectic sets. A regular at Open Ground and 1985 events, Tasha returns with her genre defying sets tinged in Jungle, D&B, Techno and more. Last but not least, Alix debuts at Open Ground for a mixed set that motions through a hybrid collection of Dubstep/Garage/Techno infused tracks, as well as deep, soulful and rolling Drum and Bass that he is primarily known for.

Paulita digs up raw disco, Brazilian funk, and slow-burning soulful house. Craig follows with deep, New York and Chicago-rooted Disco and House. Zapata brings his salsa, afro-house, and deeper pulsing house rhythms, layered with live elements and jazzy, chordier grooves.
​
Admission 30 €

makes her Open Ground debut this year, finally bringing her idiosyncratic, versatile take on dancefloor communion. “The multi-genre thing, it has to be that for me,” says
IZCO
,
Unconfined by genre but with a warm, soulful streak permeating across his work, expect IZCO to connect the UK dots between , Bruk, House, UK Garage, Grime, and Jungle.
02:00 - 06:00
Last year’s late-night set left the room changed and it turns out the feeling was mutual. Dan Snaith, known to the world as Caribou and, under his club alias, as
Daphni
, has named that very night at Open Ground among the defining influences behind his new album Butterfly, released this February. In interviews, Snaith described the club as close to his ideal listening room a space built with obsessive care for sound, and for the people in it.
That night is woven into Butterfly itself: sixteen tracks that blur the line between his two aliases more than ever before, driven by pure dancefloor instinct. Now Daphni comes back to the club that helped shape the record a full-circle set, built for the room that inspired it.

Annex:
For the first time ever,
DJ Firmeza
and
DJ Nigga Fox
go back-to-back at Open Ground on Saturday 3 October. This night gets to the heart of Lisbon's thriving Afro-Portuguese dance music scene with two masters of batida — the kuduro-born club sound forged in the city's Quinta do Mocho estate. DJ Nigga Fox is the avant-garde producer whose debut record O Meu Estilo put Príncipe on the international map, (and he carries a restless, high-voltage sound) and whose DJ sets are celebrated as psychedelic literature for the dancefloor. DJ Firmeza is a master of a unique, percussive-heavy, trance-inducing approach to the art of mixing. Expect raw, unrelenting batida and a stack of unreleased weapons.

Both artists have a home at Príncipe Discos one of Europe’s most exciting record labels. The label's co-founder José Moura says batida blew his mind the first time he heard it: "We couldn't pinpoint it. We thought, this is really something we've never heard before. It's not techno, it's not house, it's nothing that we know about.” Originating in Luanda, Angola, it evolved into a vibrant underground movement in the suburbs of Lisbon, Portugal, driven by 140 BPM rhythms blending traditional Angolan and Cape Verdean styles (like kuduro, tarraxinha, funaná, and semba) with modern techno and house production.

Admission 30 €

Annex: Cotch International is a club series, record label and curatorial platform which aims to joins the dots between global expressions of soundsystem culture, and platform emerging electronic music scenes from the margins of society. Looking at the soundsystem as a totem around which communities congregate, where resistance is solidified and new sonic and social identities are formed, Cotch has long been a pioneer of non-western club evolutions in the UK scene, operating predominately from South London over the last 10 years.

As they prepare to take over the Annex room on the 15th of August, they have prepared a special all night collaboration between Spanish trailblazer JASSS - one of the most unpredictable, breathtaking and versatile DJs currently doing it - and Cotch resident and co-founder, Joe Cotch. Taking in everything from industrial dub to blistering kuduro beats, swampy trip hop to blown-out baile funk, slinky low end psychedelia and chest-boxing basslines.. everything will be thrown in the blender as they endeavour to move your body in ways you never thought possible.

Admission 40 €

description.new:
Freifeld: Rupture has spent the last 20 years becoming London's home for deep, underground jungle and drum & bass - built on community and a refusal to commercialise the culture.
Founded in 2006 by Mantra and Double O the night was created to push the more experimental side of jungle and drum & bass.
​
By 2012 it had expanded into a record label, releasing music from artists such as Spirit, dBridge, Tim Reaper, Sully and Forest Drive West, Djinn and many more.
Rupture is widely regarded as one of London's best underground D&B nights, consistently pushing forward-thinking lineups whilst keeping community and inclusivity at its core. As the movement has evolved so has the need to double down on the essence of what it means to rave: intentional gatherings built around amazing sound systems, paying homage to the foundations of jungle and d&b whilst always looking at new ways to push the sound forward and create pathways for emerging artists.
Viva la Rave!

Annex: For the fourth time, HEAVY FEELINGS returns to the ANNEX at Open Ground, bringing together STICKY DUB from Liverpool, MOKEYANJU from Berlin and Parissa Chargi from Cologne.

Cologne-based independent platform HEAVY FEELINGS creates spaces for music, collaboration and cultural exchange. Founded by curator and creative producer PARISSA, the platform brings together artists, selectors, producers and other creative practitioners through events, radio, publishing and long-term collaborations. Rooted in DIY culture and independent artistic practice, HEAVY FEELINGS is driven by a deep belief in music as a space for connection, exchange and collective discovery.

At the centre of the lineup is Sticky Dub, a producer, MC and selector rooted in
Hip Hop
and
UK soundsystem culture
. His work moves through
Broken Beat, Dub, UK Garage, House and electronic music
, with a strong rhythmic instinct and a playful approach to genre. His releases on Eglo Records have made him a distinctive voice within the wider UK beat landscape, connecting club music, soundsystem culture and Hip Hop through his own production and selection.

Mokeyanju was part of the early circle around HEAVY FEELINGS in Cologne and returns for this edition from Berlin. A DJ, vinyl selector, interdisciplinary artist and radio host, she has developed a distinctive practice across DJing, vinyl selection, radio and interdisciplinary work. Her record collection spans Nigeria, Tanzania, Kenya, Congo, Brazil and Trinidad & Tobago, connecting
Fújì, Highlife, Benga, Soukous, Rumba, Calypso, Ndombolo, House and Electronica
. Alongside her work at Refuge Worldwide, her involvement with POETRY MEETS reflects her ongoing engagement with music, language and cultural exchange.

Completing the lineup is PARISSA, founder and curator of HEAVY FEELINGS and a Vinyl Only Selector. Her selections move through
Jazz, Dub, Afro-diasporic rhythms and electronic music
, drawing on years of digging, listening and collecting across different musical worlds. Her sets are an extension of the wider HEAVY FEELINGS practice: deeply personal selections shaped by context, curiosity and the connections between records, artists and the people in the room.
